narrativeReportMd:
# Quantity R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local R4-valid `Quantity` instance pattern was found that becomes an R6 error solely because of Quantity's own element model. The material local risks are R6-to-R4 and runtime risks: R6 adds a new required-binding comparator code `ad`, and R6 adds a best-practice warning invariant against UCUM annotation text in `Quantity.code`.

## Scope
The analysis covered the base `Quantity` datatype and its local elements: `value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code`. Inherited `Element`, `DataType`, and `Extension` changes are explicitly out of scope, including the R6 base-definition move from `Element` to `DataType`.

## Main migration themes
The structural shape of Quantity is stable: no local child elements were added, removed, renamed, moved, or retyped, and no local cardinalities changed. The main migration work is terminology-aware parsing of `Quantity.comparator` and conformance handling of the new warning constraint `qty-4`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `Quantity:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:Quantity.comparator:ad-code`: R6 permits comparator `ad` in a required binding, which R4 does not permit and older enum-based software may not understand. Because `comparator` is a modifier, silently ignoring an unknown value can change the meaning of the quantity.

## Findings requiring human review
`Quantity:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:Quantity:qty-4-warning` deserves human review in systems that intentionally use UCUM annotations or non-UCUM unit codes containing braces. R6 makes this a warning, not an error, but organizations that fail builds on warnings may see operational breaks.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Both local changes are relatively compatible for R4-to-R6 validation: the new comparator code widens an R6 terminology domain, and `qty-4` is a warning. Reverse conversion to R4 is not lossless for comparator `ad` unless an extension, custom mapping, or rejection policy is used.

## Follow-up analysis
The base datatype hierarchy change belongs to the `DataType`/`Element` reports. A cross-version terminology mapping or official rationale for comparator `ad` would improve migration guidance.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Quantity` keeps the same local element set, cardinalities, types, modifier flags, and summary flags. The top concerns are the new `Quantity.comparator` code `ad`, the R6-to-R4 lossiness of that code, and the new `qty-4` warning for coded units containing UCUM-style annotations. The largest uncertainty is rationale and recommended cross-version mapping because no official diff, ConceptMap, or narrative change note was available locally.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is primarily terminology and validator-policy work. R4 data using the existing comparator codes remains valid under the R6 required binding, but R6 data can contain `comparator: ad`, which R4 validators and generated enum models will reject. R6 validators may also warn on `Quantity.code` values with brace annotations; those annotations should generally be moved to `Quantity.unit` while keeping `Quantity.code` machine-processable.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition and CodeSystem differences because the local R4 and R6 package artifacts were compared directly. Confidence is medium for justification and prevalence because the local inputs did not include official narrative diffs, ballot rationale, terminology expansions, or cross-version ConceptMaps.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `Quantity.comparator` has the same path, id, cardinality, type, binding strength, and modifier flag in both versions; only the bound terminology version and code content changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because the old four comparator codes are still present in R6. It is a high R6-to-R4 and runtime risk because `Quantity.comparator` has a required binding and is a modifier. An R6 instance with `comparator: ad` is not valid against the R4 required binding, and older parsers or generated enum switches may reject it or, worse, ignore a modifier that changes the meaning of `value`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Quantities can affect clinical thresholds, medication strengths, inventory, and measurement interpretation. Misinterpreting or dropping a modifier comparator can change the intended quantity semantics.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent a comparator semantics where the stated value is sufficient to achieve a total quantity, not merely less-than or greater-than.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `ad` widens the R6 comparator binding and does not make any R4 comparator value invalid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: `ad` carries a distinct modifier meaning that cannot be safely collapsed into the four R4 inequality comparators. This is not a hard R4-to-R6 instance break because the R4 codes remain valid in R6; the breakage is mainly for R6-to-R4 conversion and older enum/runtime handling of new R6 content. With no official rationale in the local inputs, `Probably justified` is more appropriate than fully `Justified`, but the reported extension/backport path should not be counted as a backwards-compatible base-design alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible base alternative is applicable because the R6 base design is a widening of a required terminology domain. Modeling `ad` only in an extension would reduce failures in older R4-era consumers, but it would also demote a core modifier semantics to extension-specific handling and is best understood as a different interoperability tradeoff or reverse-conversion mitigation, not as an alternative needed to preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 extensions or conversion policy can mitigate reverse-version loss, but those are migration/backport strategies rather than less-breaking base R6 alternatives.

evidence.detail: R6 binds the same element required to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/quantity-comparator|6.0.0-ballot4`.
R4 quantity-comparator has four concepts: `<`, `<=`, `>=`, and `>`.

evidence.quote: The actual value is sufficient for the total quantity to equal the given value.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment is valid for the comparator binding only in R6. The migration example is illustrative, not a standardized cross-version extension; an implementation should use an official cross-version extension or reject the conversion if no approved mapping exists.

findings.narrativeMd: `Quantity.comparator` keeps the same 0..1 `code` shape, but the required comparator vocabulary is widened in R6 by adding `ad`. Because comparator is explicitly a modifier, this is more than an enum maintenance issue: consumers must understand whether the stated quantity is an inequality, exact/no-comparator quantity, or the new sufficient-to-achieve-total quantity semantics.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: All R4 comparator values remain valid under the R6 terminology, so this is not an old-valid/new-invalid break. The reverse direction is the problem: an R6 Quantity using `ad` is invalid in R4 because R4's required ValueSet does not contain that code. R4-era generated models with closed enums may also fail parsing, fail serialization, or drop/round-trip the unknown code incorrectly.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update Quantity comparator enums, validators, switch statements, search/index logic, and business rules to recognize `ad`. For R6-to-R4 conversion, do not map `ad` to `<`, `<=`, `>=`, or `>` because that changes semantics. Preserve it in an agreed extension, use an official ConceptMap if one becomes available, or reject/down-scope the conversion with a clear error.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backwards-compatible design could have used an optional extension to carry `ad` semantics while leaving the base required binding unchanged. That would protect R4 enum consumers but would make a core modifier meaning less discoverable and less consistently validated. Given the distinct comparator semantics, adding a code is probably justified, but it still requires explicit migration handling.

findings.title: R6 adds best-practice warning `qty-4` for UCUM-style annotations in Quantity.code

oldState.summary: R4 had the local error invariant `qty-3` requiring `system` when `code` is present, but no warning about UCUM annotations in `code`.

constraints.human: If a code for the unit is present, the system SHALL also be present

semanticText.comment: The context of use may frequently define what kind of quantity this is and therefore what kind of units can be used. The context of use may also restrict the values for the comparator.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 validates the relationship between `code` and `system` but does not locally warn about annotation text embedded in the code.

newState.summary: R6 keeps `qty-3` and adds local warning invariant `qty-4`: `code.exists() implies code.matches('\\{.*?\\}').not()`.

constraints.human: If a code for the unit is present, the system SHALL also be present
Processing UCUM codes with annotations ({..}) can be misleading.

semanticText.comment: The context of use may frequently define what kind of quantity this is and therefore what kind of units can be used. The context of use may also restrict the values for the comparator.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 introduces a best-practice warning against putting human-readable annotation content, such as UCUM brace annotations, into the machine-processable `Quantity.code`.

facts.note: R6 marks the invariant as best practice and explains that human-readable annotations should be represented in `Quantity.unit` instead.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The root `Quantity` element has the same id and path in R4 and R6. The added invariant is explicitly local to `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Quantity` in R6.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `qty-4` is a warning, not an error, so a structurally valid R4 Quantity with a brace annotation in `code` should not become invalid solely because of this invariant. It can still break operational pipelines that treat warnings as failures, and it can change conformance dashboards or quality gates. The semantic concern is real because machine unit codes with embedded human annotations can be misleading.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If a display annotation is embedded in the coded unit and then misread as part of the computable unit, quantity interpretation can be misleading. The R6 rule is intended to steer senders toward cleaner machine codes plus human-readable `unit` text.

justification.inferredGoal: Discourage UCUM annotations in `Quantity.code` and encourage human-readable annotations in `Quantity.unit`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: A less-disruptive base design could have kept the advice narrative-only or limited the warning to UCUM-coded quantities, but those alternatives would be less visible or less complete.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal is reasonable because brace annotations in a computable unit code can mislead automated processing, and R6 chose a best-practice warning rather than an error. That makes the change mostly compatible: R4 instances are not made invalid solely by `qty-4`, though warning-as-failure pipelines and non-UCUM brace conventions can still be affected. Because the plausible less-breaking alternatives materially reduce automated or complete detection, the level of breakage is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base alternatives are narrative guidance only, or a narrower invariant such as warning only when `system` is `http://unitsofmeasure.org`. Narrative-only guidance would preserve validator behavior but would be easy to miss and would not support automated conformance feedback. A UCUM-gated invariant would reduce false positives for non-UCUM unit systems, but it would not catch misleading UCUM-like annotations when `system` is absent, incorrect, or locally coded. Those tradeoffs make the alternative only partial.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Narrative-only guidance avoids warning churn but weakens automated quality checks; a UCUM-gated warning reduces false positives but can miss ambiguous codes when `system` is absent or non-standard.

evidence.detail: R4 root Quantity constraints include `qty-3` but not `qty-4`.

evidence.quote: Processing UCUM codes with annotations ({..}) can be misleading.

evidence.detail: R6 marks `qty-4` as a best-practice warning and explains that human-readable annotations should be carried by `Quantity.unit`.
evidence.quote: Best Practice is not to use annotations in the UCUM code, and rather to make sure that Quantity.unit is correctly human readable

examples.examplesMd: The first fragment illustrates data that R4 would not flag with this local Quantity warning but R6 validators may warn on. It is not expected to be an R6 error solely from `qty-4`; the migration example moves human-readable annotation into `unit` and leaves a cleaner UCUM code.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds the local `qty-4` invariant to warn when `Quantity.code` appears to contain brace-delimited annotation text. This targets a subtle semantic problem: `code` is meant to be a computable unit code, while human-readable qualification belongs in `unit`. The change can surprise teams whose historical UCUM practice used annotations such as `{...}` in the coded value.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a hard instance-breaking change because the invariant severity is `warning`. However, R4-valid instances with brace annotations can become R6-warning instances. Toolchains that fail on warnings, publish conformance scores, or treat best-practice warnings as policy violations may experience runtime or process breaks. R6-to-R4 representability is not materially reduced because R4 can still carry the same `code` string.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan Quantity instances for `code` values containing brace annotations, especially where `system` is UCUM. Prefer a valid machine code in `code` and put human-readable annotation in `unit`. If non-UCUM systems intentionally use braces, review whether local profiles or validator configuration should suppress, reinterpret, or document the warning rather than changing data blindly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: R6 chose a warning rather than an error, which is the main backward-compatible mitigation. The least disruptive alternative would be narrative guidance only, but that would be easy to miss in automated validation. A more precise alternative could make the warning conditional on the UCUM system; the current expression is broader, so human review is appropriate for non-UCUM edge cases.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The human text says UCUM, but the computable expression is only based on `code` existence and a brace-pattern match. It does not explicitly test `system = http://unitsofmeasure.org`.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: `Quantity` has the same canonical URL, id, name, type, kind, status, derivation, and abstract flag. The direct base changed from `Element` to `DataType`, but that is an inherited/base hierarchy issue and is out of scope for local findings.
The local child elements remain `value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code`; no local Quantity element was added, removed, renamed, moved, split, or merged.
`Quantity.value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code` remain 0..1. The root remains 0..* as a reusable datatype definition.
Local element types are unchanged: `value` is `decimal`, `comparator` is `code`, `unit` is `string`, `system` is `uri`, and `code` is `code`.
`Quantity` has no `Reference`-typed local elements in either version.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value was found on base `Quantity` elements in either version.

No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit changed on the Quantity element definitions themselves. The new regex-like rule is represented as warning invariant `qty-4` and is reported separately.
`Quantity.comparator` remains `isModifier=true` with the same modifier reason. Other local elements remain non-modifier.
`value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code` remain summary elements; inherited `id` and `extension` summary flags are not local findings.
No local Quantity slicing was found in either version.
Core definitions, comments, and requirements for local elements are materially stable except for the comparator short text adding `ad` and the new `qty-4` warning rationale, both covered in findings.

No local JSON/XML representation change was found for `Quantity.value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, or `code`. Inherited XML attribute and global constraint XPath metadata differences were excluded as base/tooling-scope issues.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 snapshot marks Quantity.code as participating in `qty-3`
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The underlying invariant `qty-3` already existed in R4 with the same error expression `code.empty() or system.exists()`. R6 adding `qty-3` to the `Quantity.code` condition metadata makes the linkage more explicit but does not create a new validation rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that display constraint-to-element relationships may show `qty-3` on `Quantity.code` in R6 even though the validation obligation is not new.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 comparator binding includes an additional binding-definition extension
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The added extension carries descriptive tooling metadata for the binding; it does not change cardinality, type, binding strength, or validation beyond the terminology content reported separately.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: StructureDefinition consumers that preserve ElementDefinition extensions may see an extra extension at the comparator binding, but instance serialization is unchanged.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 changes `Quantity.baseDefinition` from `Element` to `DataType`. This report excludes that inherited hierarchy shift; the DataType/Element reports should assess its cross-cutting codegen and inheritance effects.
The new R6 comparator code `ad` has no R4 equivalent in the local terminology inputs. A ConceptMap or official cross-version extension policy would determine safe R6-to-R4 conversion behavior.
